Applicants must meet the following Basic Education requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: A. Degree: Engineering.

To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.

OR B.

Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering.

The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1 , or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico.

Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration.

For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2.

Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico. 3.

Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A.

The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A. 4.

Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.

Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.

(The above examples of related curricula are not all inclusive.) Note: An applicant who meets the basic requirements as specified in A or B above, except as noted under B.1., may qualify for positions in any branch of engineering unless selective factors indicate otherwise.

Qualifying experience may have been acquired in any public or private sector job, but will clearly demonstrate past experience in the application of the particular competencies or knowledge, skills and abilities necessary to successfully perform the duties of the position.

Such experience is typically in or directly related to the work of the position to be filled.

Electrical Designer As an Electrical Designer, you will support various phases of project development, including planning, site evaluations, analytical design, proposal documentation, report generation, specification development, and preparation of construction documents and electrical drawings.

This role will take the lead on diverse projects across multiple sectors, contributing to a wide range of design efforts for a variety of clients.

Key Responsibilities Design a broad range of electrical systems, including schematics, grid layouts, electrical power distribution, lighting, protection and control systems, and site/facility electrical layouts. Adhere to all applicable design, drafting, and documentation standards set by the company, clients, and specific projects.

Plan and prepare drawing packages for production, including conducting analysis, developing layouts, and performing complex calculations on non-routine assignments. Complete electrical design tasks using standard techniques, such as determining drawing sequences, component sizing, and refining initial sketches.

Revise existing designs or drawings based on redlines or mark-ups during project execution. Analyze drawings, test data, and technical reports to support project planning and design decisions. Interpret and apply design codes and technical specifications to meet project requirements.

Review design documents for quality, consistency, and accuracy while staying within scope, schedule, and budget constraints. Perform calculations for conduit fill, grounding layouts, wiring diagrams, and relay panel schematics.

Organize and manage project drawings, revision history, plot files, and related documentation in a structured, accessible format. Communicate clearly and effectivelyboth verbally and in writingwhen coordinating with project teams and clients. Perform additional duties as needed in alignment with project and company objectives.

Qualifications Bachelors degree in drafting technology or a related field and at least 7 years of relevant experience; OR Associate degree with a minimum of 8 years of experience; OR 9 years of progressive design and detailing experience in lieu of a degree. Advanced proficiency in design software such as AutoCAD, MicroStation, and Microsoft Excel.

Strong aptitude for learning and applying new design tools and technologies. Experience with both 2D and 3D design applications; SmartPlant 3D experience is strongly preferred. Advanced understanding of electrical design principles, calculations, and systems.

Broad knowledge of engineering practices across disciplines and the ability to use discipline-specific software for design execution. Proven ability to work collaboratively with multidisciplinary project teams including engineers, project managers, and fellow designers to resolve design issues. Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Strong analytical thinking, problem-solving ability, and a sharp eye for detail. Originally posted on Himalayas

Your mission We are seeking a highly skilled Senior High-Voltage Airborne Electronics Engineer (all genders) to design, develop, and validate high-performance power control and conversion hardware. The ideal candidate will have strong expertise in power electronics design, component selection, simulation, PCB design, testing, and will work closely with cross-functional teams to deliver reliable, efficient, and cost-effective power solutions.
Your Day-to-Day Design and develop power electronics hardware including power distribution & protection units, solid-state power controllers and DC-DC converters.
Capture requirements and manage them systematically in a traceable way.
Create schematics, PCB layouts, and BOMs for power electronic systems.
Perform circuit analysis, simulations, and design optimization (thermal, EMI/EMC, efficiency, reliability).
Select and qualify power components such as Power MOSFETs, IGBTs, SiC / GaN devices, magnetics, and passive components.
Lead prototype build, bring-up, debugging, and validation testing.
Conduct failure analysis and implement design improvements.
Ensure compliance with relevant safety and regulatory standards (UL, IEC, ISO, etc.).
Collaborate with firmware, mechanical, manufacturing, procurement and quality teams.
Support production ramp-up, manufacturing test development, and field issue resolution.
Prepare and maintain technical documentation, test reports, and design reviews.
Your profile Bachelor's or master's degree in electrical engineering or related field.
More than 5 years of professional experience.
Strong background in power electronics theory and practical hardware design.
Experience with electrical protection, power semiconductors, converter topologies and control methods.
Proficiency in schematic capture and PCB design tools such as Altium Designer ( preferred ), OrCAD, or KiCad .
Hands-on experience with lab equipment (oscilloscopes, power supplies, power analysers, electronic loads).
Solid understanding of electronics packaging, thermal management, EMI/EMC, and safety design.
Ability to debug complex hardware issues independently.
Experience with wide bandgap semiconductors ( SiC , GaN ).
Familiarity with simulation tools (LTspice, PLECS, PSIM, MATLAB/Simulink).
Knowledge of high-voltage and high-power systems.
Experience with testing hardware under high-voltage (>800V).
Experience with DO-254 process.
Experience with aerospace & defence standards (DO-160, MIL-STD-810, MIL-STD-461, MIL-STD-704).
A valid (car) driving licence is preferred for occasional travel between our locations .

Written Test - Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination, or any other written test required for professional registration, by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico.3.

Specified academic courses - Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in A above. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program.4.

Related curriculum - Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.

Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.

In addition to meeting the Individual Occupational Requirement (IOR), applicants must meet the following specialized experience: Applicants must have 52 weeks of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level, GS-9 in the Federal Service.

Specialized Experience is the experience that equipped the applicant with the particular knowledge, skills, and abilities (KSA's) to perform the duties of the position successfully, and that is typically in or related to the position to be filled.

To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the next lower grade level. Qualifying specialized experience for GS-11 includes: Participating in technical training in the area of calibration procedures or other technically related activities. Assisting in the design of electronic circuit modifications.

Developing, implementing or troubleshooting mechanical and/or electronic systems used for calibration. Implementing quality control and/or quality assurance programs for the calibration of equipment.

OR Education: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as General Engineering; Mechanical Engineering; Electronics Engineering; or Electrical Engineering.

(Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position.

Mission Brief
Join the Avionics Department at Isar, within the Electrical Engineering Team responsible for high‑reliability hardware design of PCBAs and Avionics Units that are the backbone of our Spectrum Launch Vehicle.
As a Senior Avionics Engineer, you will provide direct contribution to our technology stack and take responsibility for critical Avionics units: driving them through their entire lifecycle from early concept, to detailed design, qualification, and all the way to successful on-orbit operations in Space.
The ideal candidate is someone with deep technical expertise in Electrical and Electronics engineering who thrives in a fast-moving environment. Preference will be given to those with the ability to make sound technical decisions, able to raise the bar for engineering quality, and the ability to provide technical mentorship to other Engineers along the way.

s.h: Your Role in Our Space Mission
s.t:
Take on ownership of at least one high-reliability Avionics Unit
Own all interfaces of your product across its lifecycle, from design to manufacturing to verification and integration, including all technical and programmatic interfaces
Carry out the full Electrical design cycle for PCBAs including component selection, schematic capture, layout and design verification
Take on Unit level tasks for your products including requirement management, design, reliability analyses, qualification & acceptance testing, as well as troubleshooting analysis
Conduct design reviews for your products and participate in system level design reviews
Plan, execute, and evaluate verification, acceptance, and qualification tests at unit, subsystem, and vehicle level
Develop test procedures and automated scripts for verifying unit functional and electrical performance under harsh operating conditions, such as thermal, vacuum, and vibration
Capture interface requirements and design specifications for test equipment used in test campaigns of your products
Actively participate in Integrated Testing & Flight Data reviews
Collaborate on ad-hoc tasks related to Avionics PCBAs, Units and, Systems with your peers in the Avionics department

Our mission is to help democratise space and use it for good in order to improve life on Earth now and for the future generations.
We are a fast-growing company aiming to provide sustainable and environmentally friendly launch solutions for small and medium-sized satellites and constellations into Low Earth Orbit. Preparing complex electrical load analyses, fault current analyses, and coordination of protective devices for proposed shipboard alterations.
Developing contract designs and in-house designs while performing troubleshooting and First Article Testing in accordance with regulatory agency standards.
Conducting surveys, inspection trips, and attending sea trials or ship checks before, during, and after structural and system alterations.
Performing Electrical Calculations and Schematics, including Voltage Drop Calculations, Load Calculations, and Power & Lighting One Line Diagrams.
Developing Electrical Plant Load Analysis (EPLA), Protective Device Coordination Studies, and Electric Plant Distribution Impact Data (EPDID).
Collaborating with stakeholders to develop Failure Modes and Effects Analyses (FMEA) and Periodic Safety Test Procedures (PSTP) for U.S. Coast Guard approvals.
Working with all internal and external teams to ensure complete and functioning electrical systems that meet all MSC mission requirements.
Occasional travel to Chesapeake or Norfolk, VA, for client meetings and events.

Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field
5+ years of experience with specialized vessels in one or more of the following areas: Expeditionary Fast Transport Vessels (T-EPF), Hospital Ships (T-AH), Dry Cargo/Ammunition Ships (T-AKE), Underway Replenishment Oilers (T-AO), Cable Laying/Repair (T-ARC), Rescue/Salvage Ships (T-ARS), Submarine Tender (T-AS), Fleet Ocean Tugs (T-ATF), Command Ship (LCC), Expeditionary Mobile Base (T-ESB), Fast Combat Support Vessels (T-AOE) or like vessels.
Experience with marine power plants, propulsion control systems, automation and control systems, and electrical/lighting distribution systems.
Experience with navigation and marine electronics systems in a naval or merchant marine environment.

Demonstrated experience developing Failure Modes and Effects Analyses (FMEA) and Periodic Safety Test Procedures (PSTP).
Proficiency with SKM (or similar power system analysis software), MathCAD, Adobe Pro, AutoCAD, and MS Office Suite.
Self-starter with excellent people skills - able to work across teams, organize meetings/boards, and drive change throughout an organization.
An active Secret clearance is required for this position.

Must be able to remain in a stationary position 50% of the time.
Needs to occasionally move about inside the office to access file cabinets, climb ladder wells on vessels, etc.
Frequently communicates with co-workers, management, and customers, which may involve attending meetings.

Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!
Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.
We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.
It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.
🐙 Kraken Generation Flex
The energy industry is undergoing the largest transformation since industrialisation, at an unprecedented rate of change and we are positioning ourselves at the heart of it. In Germany, home to the largest electricity market in Europe and a roadmap toward Net Zero by 2045, we are scaling rapidly to integrate Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into the grid.
Kraken is recognised as a thought leader and innovator. We are building a SaaS business that digitally connects hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets. As we expand our footprint in Germany and the wider European market, we are looking for a Senior Electrical Engineer to lead our regional technical market-access and integration efforts.

s.h: 🏠 Where you’ll fit in and role summary
s.t:
As we enter a stage of rapid commercialisation and customer growth in Germany, we are looking for a Senior Electrical Engineer to work with stakeholders to develop our DSR (Demand Side Response) and flexibility pipeline.
You will be bringing your regional technical expertise to aid the development of our asset integration technologies. The role is highly cross-functional: you'll bridge our software and hardware capabilities with the rigorous requirements of the four German Transmission System Operators (TSOs) and 900+ Distribution System Operators (DSOs).
The detailed Gateway (Kraken’s IoT Edge Hardware&Software) configuration and protocol engineering is owned by our UK-based team, whom you will feed with regional knowledge and design input, and who will support you on the technical aspects of how Kraken integrations work.

You will own the regional relationship, the integration approach, and the design that the UK team then implements. The role may require you to attend customer calls, as well as calls with the TSO and DSOs to technically explain/defend our strategy.
You will join a team, based in Manchester, that is innovative and engineering-focused, with a culture that fosters collaboration and fresh thinking to create a new energy system.
🚀 What you'll own
Market Access & Prequalification: Drive the technical approach for connecting assets — mainly BESS (grid-scale and C&I) and RES (Wind and Solar) into German ancillary-service markets (FCR, aFRR, mFRR) and Redispatch 3.0.

Support prequalification (Präqualifikation) with the relevant TSO and ensure our telemetry and control approach satisfies TSO-specific and BNetzA requirements for market participation. (Grid-code and plant-compliance obligations such as VDE-AR-N 4110/4120 remain with the plant/PPC; your focus is enabling market access, telemetry, and dispatch.)
Integration Technology (your core deliverable): Carry out research, engage technical stakeholders and engineers to design our established integration approaches for various asset types such as BESS, Wind, Solar, CHP and more. This can cover both new projects and retrofits.
Regional Technical Expertise: Be the regional authority who feeds and supports the UK team with knowledge of German hardware requirements, industrial protocols, connectivity, cyber-security expectations, and TSO/DSO and ancillary-service requirements. Help evaluate hardware and connectivity solutions for regional fit.
Stakeholder Liaison: Act as the technical point of contact for TSOs, DSOs, customers, and internal commercial teams to resolve connection, onboarding, or operational issues.
Hardware & On-site Support (occasional): Hardware is deployed remotely in most cases via O&Ms and third parties. However, occasional regional support and hands-on intervention may be required before or after a deployment, including some hardware handling and on-site engineering. You’ll ideally be based close to Kraken’s Berlin office and the role requires the ability to travel when needed, though this is kept to a minimum.

s.h: 🧠 What you'll bring to the party
s.t:
Language: Native or professional fluency in German and English , essential for technical documentation and TSO/regulator communication.
Engineering background: Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering, Automation/Control, or a related field ( or equivalent practical experience in industrial/energy integration).
Integration & connectivity: Proven experience establishing industrial communication and connectivity between field equipment and external systems (telemetry and/or control).
Power-plant systems: Working understanding of power-plant control systems and instrumentation, including metering.

TSO/DSO hierarchy and the connection/integration process.
Ancillary services (FCR, aFRR, mFRR) prequalification and technical requirements.
Redispatch 3.0 regulatory framework.
Customer-facing delivery: Ability to produce technical integration approaches and communicate them to customers, regulators, and internal teams.
Travel: Occasional travel may be required.
A drive to get things done in a collaborative, agile environment , comfortable navigating the complexity of a multi-TSO, decentralised grid, and comfortable being the regional face of a technical function whose deep build sits with a partner team in the UK.

Knowledge of industrial communication protocols: IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61400-25 (wind), OPC-UA, Modbus , or similar IEC protocols.
Understanding of IT/OT security in the energy sector ( NIS2, EnWG/KRITIS awareness ; IEC 62443 a plus).
Familiarity with CLI tools for configuring, diagnosing, and maintaining hardware or network connections in remote, Linux-based environments.
Familiarity with software languages, version-controlled configuration, and general tooling.
Exposure to the wider European balancing markets / ENTSO-E frameworks beyond Germany.

To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.- OR B.

Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering.

The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1, or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico.

Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration.

For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions.

Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.

Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A.

The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A.

Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.

(The above examples of related curricula are not all-inclusive.) Specialized experience is professional engineering experience assisting with engineering and scientific work involving electrical circuits, circuit elements, electrical equipment/ systems, and associated phenomena concerned with electromagnetic wave energy or electrical information; and includes experience of electric power (EP) theories, concepts, principles, methods, applications, tools, and practices related to EP and/or supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) operations and modeling and simulation (M&S).
